import nki
import nki.isa as nisa
import nki.language as nl

@nki.jit
def tensor_avgpool_kernel(x, pool_size):
    C, H, W = x.shape
    p = pool_size
    out_shape = (C, H // p, W // p)
    out = nl.ndarray(out_shape, dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
    tile = nl.ndarray((C, H, W), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x)
    
    # Compute the average over the pooling window
    # Reshape to (C, H//p, p, W//p, p)
    # Then compute mean over the last two dimensions
    # We use tile views and reductions to achieve this
    # First, reshape the tile to (C, H//p, p, W//p, p)
    # We'll use a strided view to simulate the reshape
    # The tile is (C, H, W), and we want to view it as (C, H//p, p, W//p, p)
    # So we need to compute the strides and counts accordingly
    
    # Compute the number of tiles along H and W
    num_h_tiles = H // p
    num_w_tiles = W // p
    
    # We'll compute the mean over the last two dimensions (p x p)
    # So we'll reduce over the last two dimensions
    # We'll use a nested loop to iterate over the tiles
    # First, iterate over the C dimension (partition axis)
    for c in nl.affine_range(C):
        # Iterate over the H dimension (tiles)
        for h in nl.affine_range(num_h_tiles):
            # Iterate over the W dimension (tiles)
            for w in nl.affine_range(num_w_tiles):
                # Compute the start and end indices for the pooling window
                start_h = h * p
                start_w = w * p
                end_h = start_h + p
                end_w = start_w + p
                # Extract the pooling window
                window = tile[c, start_h:end_h, start_w:end_w]
                # Compute the mean of the window
                mean = nl.sum(window, axis=[1, 2], keepdims=True) / (p * p)
                # Store the result in the output
                out[c, h, w] = mean
    return out
